clue.text: Trial marriages for top batsmen?

definitions.note: the definition describes what the matches are for: games for the best cricketers

parts.note: a trial is a test
marriages are matches, as in a good match

explanation.surface: A whimsical suggestion that leading cricketers should try out their weddings first.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the top international fixtures are five-day games between national sides, the highest level a batsman plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket's international five-day fixtures are where the best batters are picked to play.

clue.text: Shocking weather!

parts.note: read literally, weather that delivers shocks: thunder and lightning rather than merely awful conditions

explanation.definitionFit: Lightning-filled tempests are weather that literally shocks, carrying electrical charge.

clue.text: Excessively long implement

parts.note: excessively means too, as in too much

explanation.surface: An implement that is far too long to be useful.
explanation.definitionFit: An implement is a device or instrument used for a job, like a spanner.

clue.text: Extinct mollusc shells, dark, we hear

parts.note: shells are ammunition, ammo for short

indicators.note: we hear tells us the word for dark is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: dark as a noun means night-time, the night

explanation.surface: Shells of a vanished mollusc, said to be dark in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shells' looks like part of the mollusc picture but it is the ammunition.
explanation.definitionFit: This coiled fossil cephalopod died out with the dinosaurs.

clue.text: Rumour of eccentric swallowing sodium

indicators.note: swallowing means one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or comical person
Na is the chemical symbol for sodium

explanation.surface: Gossip spread by an odd character who has eaten salt.
explanation.definitionFit: A canard is a false report or unfounded story, a hoax rumour.

clue.text: Rare oath, for example, these days

parts.note: AD, anno domini, is the era of these days

explanation.surface: A seldom-heard swear word, for example nowadays.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an old-fashioned mild exclamation, a minced form of 'by God', now seldom used.

clue.text: Cover is quicker in this excellent position

definitions.text: Cover is quicker in this excellent position

parts.words: Cover is quicker in this excellent position
parts.note: read as postal service, an envelope or cover travels faster by the premium class of mail; read as cricket, it sounds like a fielding spot

explanation.walkthrough: Cover is a cricket fielding position, and also a philatelist's word for a stamped envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's premium mail grade moves a letter faster, ideally next day.

clue.text: Righteous anger of the people, following popular excavation

indicators.note: following means the people come after the other pieces

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
a dig is an archaeological excavation
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Public fury at a much-loved archaeological dig.
explanation.definitionFit: Indignation is anger aroused by something seen as unjust or unfair.

clue.text: Plug cracking up

definitions.meaning: a plug is a piece of promotion or endorsement
to crack something up is to praise it highly

explanation.definitionFit: A favourable mention puffing something is endorsement, praise offered to others.

clue.text: A Cornishman, perhaps, out of his time?

definitions.note: the definition says a person displaced from his own era

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters given might be some other arrangement

explanation.surface: A man from Cornwall who seems to belong to another era.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan's 'Comishman' is RN read as M; Cornwall is England's far south-western county.
explanation.definitionFit: Something belonging to a period other than the one it appears in is chronologically misplaced.

clue.text: Return of school register

indicators.note: return of means the school's name is read backwards

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Bringing back a school's attendance register.
explanation.definitionFit: To register something is to notice or take heed of it.

clue.text: Minute opening

definitions.meaning: a minute is a record written in a log or the minutes of a meeting
an opening is a way in, a doorway

explanation.definitionFit: Both a recorded item in a log and a doorway or way in carry this name.

clue.text: A second italian coming back for wine

indicators.note: coming back means the drink's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and it

explanation.surface: A man from Italy returns briefly for a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'italian' looks like a person but it is the vermouth, the 'it' of 'gin and it'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sparkling white from Piedmont is a well-known wine.

clue.text: Pass along the border

definitions.meaning: to pass along the edge of something is to go round it
a border is an edge or fringe

explanation.definitionFit: Going round the edge and an outer fringe both share this word.

clue.text: Vaughan Williams, so-called in his orchestral phase

indicators.note: in means the name sits within the words that follow

explanation.surface: The English composer is named in his period of orchestral writing.
explanation.walkthrough: Vaughan Williams was an English composer whose first name was famously pronounced 'Rafe'.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer Vaughan Williams bore this first name.

clue.text: Chirpy creatures with constant symptoms of vitamin D deficiency

parts.note: c is the symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light
rickets is the bone-softening disease caused by lack of vitamin D

explanation.surface: Cheerful animals that suffer persistently from a vitamin shortage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chirpy' looks like cheerful but means literally chirping insects.
explanation.definitionFit: These insects make a chirping noise by rubbing their wings.

clue.text: English river-study to find bird of prey

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: Studying an English river turns up a raptor.
explanation.definitionFit: This raptor is a fast hunting hawk with long pointed wings.

clue.text: Loud bunch laid up on a small fleet

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical direction for loud
a lot is a bunch or group
laid up means ill in bed

explanation.surface: A noisy group, bedridden, aboard a little fleet.
explanation.definitionFit: A flotilla is a group of small ships, a modest naval squadron.

clue.text: Habitually go to Brighton, for example?

definitions.meaning: to go often to a place, or turn to it as a habit
Brighton is a seaside town on England's south coast, a holiday destination

explanation.definitionFit: Frequenting a place and a seaside holiday town share this word.

clue.text: The plane crash one always remembers, reportedly

indicators.note: crash suggests the letters given are wrecked and rearranged

explanation.surface: A plane crash so terrible that it is never forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying goes that this beast never forgets; 'reportedly' marks it as folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbially the largest land mammal never forgets.

clue.text: Road curve — note traffic light!

parts.note: C is a musical note
amber is the middle colour on a traffic light

explanation.surface: A bend on the road where a traffic signal deserves attention.
explanation.definitionFit: A road's camber is its slight convex rise from edge to crown, to drain water.

clue.text: Sheltered corner without a green light

parts.note: no means without, as in no money
a green light is approval, an OK

explanation.surface: A secluded spot that has not yet been given permission.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosy recess or secluded spot is a snug little alcove.

clue.text: Irascible riparian

definitions.meaning: riparian means riverbank-dwelling, like the water vole of Wind in the Willows

explanation.walkthrough: In Kenneth Grahame's The Wind in the Willows the riverbank-dwelling water vole bears this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Both bad-tempered and the riverside creature of Grahame's tale carry this word.

clue.text: Capital consists of mostly loose change

indicators.note: change means the remaining letters are rearranged
mostly means the word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A city is made up largely of coins in your pocket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose change' looks like coins; 'mostly' cuts LOOSE to LOOS, which 'change' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norwegian capital city.

clue.text: Home fixture for city

definitions.meaning: a bathtub is a fixture in a house
a Somerset city famous for its Roman spa

explanation.definitionFit: Both a tub plumbed into a house and a Georgian spa city in Somerset take this name.

clue.text: Circular letters about non-drinking German king

indicators.note: about means one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: o is a circular letter, here two of them
TT means teetotal

explanation.surface: Leaflets sent around about abstaining from drink, sent to a German monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Several medieval Holy Roman Emperors and German kings bore this name, Otto the Great among them.

clue.text: Lady Macbeth's trouble, giving bonus to mailman

indicators.note: giving here means yielding, the letters bend into a new shape

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's queen has a problem: tipping the postman.
explanation.walkthrough: In Macbeth, Lady Macbeth walks in her sleep, trying to wash blood off her hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepwalking is what afflicts Lady Macbeth in Act 5 of the play.

clue.text: Unusual, Thoreau's web site?

indicators.note: unusual suggests the letters are put in a strange order

parts.note: the possessive s counts here as a letter

explanation.surface: A peculiar online page belonging to the American writer Thoreau.
explanation.walkthrough: 'website' must be split: WEB is fodder, 'site' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's location or position is their site.
